problem:
The entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & k \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
equals $-1$ and $det(A)=4-2k.$ Find the value of $k.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix Using the Cofactor Method

feedback.problem:
The entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & k & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]$
equals $\frac{1}{18}$ and $det(A)=-18.$ Find the value of $k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=-18
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{31}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{31} & =(-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ k & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ k & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2+k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{13}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{31} \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}\cdot (2+k).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{13}^{′}=\frac{1}{18}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{18}(2+k) & =\frac{1}{18} \\ 2+k & =-1 \\ k & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
